message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001299","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity is acceptable across the list: all candidates align on cervical cancer/cervical carcinoma in trait_reported/trait_efo, and phenotyping_reported is a direct disease endpoint (often incident cervical cancer), which is considered a strong direct-match signal (prs_model_evaluator trait_labels section). For ranking, the most comparable evidence is PRS-only performance when available (prs_model_evaluator performance_metrics section). PGS001299 is the only candidate providing explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.552 and PGS R² (no covariates)=0.00263) plus incremental AUROC, making its standalone genetic contribution interpretable; most other candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index with additional epidemiologic covariates (e.g., parity, oral contraceptive use, smoking), which can inflate discrimination and is not a reliable substitute for PRS-only performance. The heritability lookup for 'cervical cancer' returned a UKBB self-reported cervical cancer record with very low observed h2 (~0.00011; liability ~0.0020), which supports interpreting the modest PRS-only R² from PGS001299 as plausible and cautions against over-weighting higher full-model AUROC values that may be largely covariate-driven (prs_model_evaluator performance_metrics heritability sanity-check guidance)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS005271","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Skill guidance applied (prs_model_evaluator skill_overview + performance-metrics principles): all candidates are direct endpoint matches (trait_efo=Hashimoto’s thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported/trait_reported=lymphocytic thyroiditis) and are siblings from the same 2026 medRxiv multi-ancestry study with the same validation N (94,651) and evaluation ancestry mix. None reports PRS-only AUC/R2; only full-model AUROC is shown with covariates listed as Unknown, so small AUROC differences (0.639 vs 0.630 vs 0.605) are not a robust basis for ranking across models when covariate contribution is unclear. In this situation, the skill recommends leaning on structural signals and effect-size evidence: PGS005271 (PRS-CS; ~1.09M variants) has the strongest per-SD effect size (OR≈1.55) among the candidates, consistent with better standalone PRS discrimination than PGS005272 (OR≈1.42) and especially PGS005270 (OR≈1.04), while also using a modern genome-wide Bayesian method rather than a sparse P+T score (55 variants). Heritability sanity-check was performed via get_heritability_records for ‘hashimoto's thyroiditis’ but returned no matching local h2 records, so no h2-based ceiling/context can be applied; confidence is therefore moderate rather than high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002082","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS Model Evaluator procedural overview (skill_overview): prioritize endpoint fidelity, PRS evidence comparability/cleanliness, method/structure, and transportability signals rather than full-model AUC alone. For target trait lupus erythematosus, PGS002082 is the best direct match because it uses the exact EFO label (lupus erythematosus) and a broad phenotype definition (localized and systemic), whereas many alternatives are narrower SLE subphenotypes (early-onset, nephritis, renal onset) or have endpoint/covariate packaging concerns (e.g., PGS003960 includes a phenotype risk score covariate, making its high full-model AUROC less interpretable as standalone PRS quality). Structurally, PGS002082 is a modern genome-wide LDpred2 score with large development sample size (n=391,124) and dense variant coverage (361,553), which are positive signals for polygenic signal capture and robustness when PRS-only AUC/R2 are not reported across the candidate set. Heritability sanity-check: local EUR records for systemic lupus erythematosus show substantial SNP-heritability (h2≈0.64; liability h2≈0.21, LDSC), supporting that a genome-wide PRS is plausible for this trait family and making PGS002082’s modest PRS-focused partial correlation evidence (partial-r=0.0212 in EUR) credible for a broad EHR-derived lupus endpoint."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002037","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches to the target via trait_efo = nicotine dependence, with consistent trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = Tobacco use disorder, so endpoint fidelity is acceptable. Following prs_model_evaluator guidance (read_skill_section: skill_overview and performance_metrics), when candidates come from the same study family and lack PRS-only AUC/R2, small metric differences are not decisive and we should weigh structural signals (method family, variant coverage) plus the best available PRS-comparable metric. Here, PGS002037 uses LDpred2 with far broader variant coverage (847,691 vs 13,838) and shows a higher partial correlation in European validation (partial-r 0.0741 vs 0.0557) under similar basic covariates and the same training/validation context, making it the stronger pick. Trait heritability was checked with get_heritability_records for both “nicotine dependence” and the close label “tobacco use disorder,” but no matching EUR h2 records were returned; therefore h2 cannot further contextualize the observed partial-r and confidence remains Moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000082","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS Model Evaluator framework (read_skill_section: skill_overview + performance_metrics): prioritize endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), then compare performance evidence with attention to PRS-only vs full-model metrics and covariate packaging.

Endpoint fidelity: Target is ovarian neoplasm. The closest exact EFO matches are the PRSweb models (PGS000544–PGS000564; trait_efo ovarian neoplasm), but their observed discrimination is consistently weak (full-model AUROC ~0.52–0.57; pseudo-R² mostly ~0.002–0.011) in small evaluations (~5,196). Several other candidates are narrower/special-population endpoints (BRCA1/2 carriers or specific histologic subtypes), which are less appropriate for a general “ovarian neoplasm” target.

Best overall trade-off: PGS000082 (ovarian cancer; incident ovarian cancer) is a close malignant-ovary endpoint match and has the strongest overall evidence among general-population ovarian cancer scores in this list: very large European evaluation (n=211,958) and the best reported discrimination in that broadly matched set (AUROC ~0.656 / C-index ~0.655). Per the performance_metrics guidance, these are full-model metrics with substantial covariates, so they are not treated as pure PRS-only performance; however, given the much weaker performance of the exact-label PRSweb scores and the narrower scope of BRCA/subtype scores, PGS000082 remains the most defensible single pick.

Heritability sanity check (get_heritability_records): no EUR h2 records matched “ovarian neoplasm”. A broader lookup for “ovarian cancer” returned only non-cancer ovarian conditions (ovarian cysts/PCOS), so h2 is not directly informative for malignant ovarian neoplasm here and does not change the selection; it mainly reinforces caution about over-interpreting full-model AUROC as PRS-only performance."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000024","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Skill grounding (read_skill_section: skill_overview, performance_metrics, publication_context): For within-trait selection, prioritize endpoint fidelity, then PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUC/R2 when available), and discount covariate-inflated full-model AUROC; publication context mainly helps identify framework vs disease-focused studies.

Why PGS000024: It is directly aligned to type 1 diabetes (trait_efo matches; phenotyping_reported is Type 1 diabetes) and comes from a disease-focused Diabetes Care paper explicitly developing/standardizing an improved T1D genetic risk score. It has strong reported discrimination in the selected European validation record (full-model AUROC 0.921) and exceptionally large reported validation size (n≈374,000), which supports robustness. While covariates are listed as “Unknown” (so AUROC may not be strictly PRS-only), the record does not show the clear biomarker-heavy packaging seen in PGS000021 (which includes islet auto-antibody status plus BMI and age at diagnosis, and shows a large drop from AUROC 0.96 to 0.87 without covariates—consistent with covariate inflation per the performance_metrics guidance).

Why not the main alternatives: (i) PGS000021’s very high AUROC is partly driven by near-outcome clinical covariates (autoantibodies), making its full-model AUROC less comparable as a standalone PGS. (ii) Pan-trait / framework-derived UKB scores with explicit PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS001297: PGS-only AUROC ~0.77, PGS-only R2 ~0.091) are informative, but publication_context guidance warns these frameworks are not reliably optimized for a specific disease; here they also do not clearly outperform the disease-focused T1D GRS evidence on the record. (iii) The 2023 “five biobanks” candidates include a MultiPRS (PGS004162) with higher reported R2, but they are trained on a very small stated training N (n=804) and are benchmarking/ensemble context; given the mixed comparability of full-model R2/AUC across designs, I prefer the disease-focused, large-validation T1D GRS.

Heritability sanity-check (get_heritability_records: type 1 diabetes mellitus): EUR h2 records for “Type 1 Diabetes” vary substantially by source/phenotype definition (e.g., GWAS Atlas h2 ~0.15–0.38 vs much lower observed-scale UKBB LDSC estimates for UKB-coded T1D). This variability supports being cautious about over-interpreting any single UKB-derived PRS-only metric and favors a T1D-specific score with strong external/large-scale validation evidence in the candidate metadata.

Net: PGS000024 best balances direct endpoint alignment with strong, robust validation signals while avoiding the clearest covariate-leakage pattern in the top-AUROC alternative."}
